minutes.headline: Select Board ratified three hires, heard ARPA pitches and PFAS well-testing talk, and reviewed the assessing investigation findings.
minutes.summary: The board ratified the Council on Aging assistant, a temporary conservation administrator and a facility superintendent, and approved a utility pole petition, a DBA change, a cemetery gift and an easement. It heard an ARPA pitch from the cultural council and met with the Board of Health about PFAS testing of private wells; no allocations were made. Late in the night members discussed the tax investigation's core-question answers and dog-hearing procedure, and set a Zoom meeting for an assessor appointment.

public_comment.topic: Urged residents, especially women, to consider joining the board of assessors and spoke about exemptions.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to ratify the facility superintendent appointment, unanimously, along with appointments to the Council on Aging and conservation.
The board ratified a Council on Aging administrative assistant and a temporary conservation administrator, then approved a utility pole petition and a restaurant name change.
The board heard an ARPA pitch from the cultural council and met the Board of Health on PFAS in private wells; no allocations were made.
Members agreed to redo the ARPA rankings so every member rates the same items, and to hold a remote meeting to appoint an interim assessor.
The chair is to revise the tax investigation report with recommendations for the September meeting, and the board accepted a permanent and temporary easement.

why_it_matters: ARPA federal funds are still unallocated, so requests such as PFAS response for the water district and private-well help are competing for a limited pot that the board has not yet ranked consistently.
The Board of Health reported little budget for helping homeowners pay for private-well testing or treatment, so for now those costs may fall on the household.
An interim appointment to the board of assessors and the tax investigation's recommendations bear on who sets property valuations and how abatements are handled in the tax rate.
watch_next: The remote meeting set for next Wednesday at 5:30 to appoint an interim assessor.
The September 5 meeting, which will cover only the dog hearing and ARPA, and the revised tax investigation report.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the four ratification/gift/pole-petition votes and most headline figures, but our minutes list three votes the official minutes do not record: the conservation administrator appointment, the DBA name change and the easement. Our minutes also list a few figures and decisions the official minutes lack or word differently, and the official minutes' own pole number and attendee names are rendered differently from ours.
